clue.text: A must for 1/4, proof all infantry's heading for review?

definitions.meaning: on the first of April (1/4 in British date order) ... is necessarily over and done with

definitions.text: proof all infantry's heading for review?
definitions.meaning: a parade in which troops file by a saluting officer for inspection

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue that seems to promise the April Fool answer while describing soldiers parading.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1/4 tag tempts the solver to write in APRIL FOOL, but that answer lives at 23/24; here 1/4 is the date, the first of April, by which March has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A march past is a military parade reviewed by a dignitary; on 1 April the month of March has elapsed.

clue.text: Chopper's fallen on toe of Hammer film director

indicators.note: an axe falling on the toe lops off the final letter

parts.note: a mallet is a hammer

explanation.surface: An axe drops on the foot of a director of Hammer horror films.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer Films is the British studio famed for horror, so 'Hammer film director' reads as one phrase; Hammer is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Malle was a French filmmaker, the director of Au Revoir les Enfants.

clue.text: Romantic country sport played in tiara

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, set in a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby match takes place in a tiara-wearing kingdom of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' rearranges IN and TIARA into RITANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional Central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's adventure romance The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Old bit of dry grass cut by writer before noon

indicators.note: the grass is cut open by the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: the writer comes before noon in the inserted letters

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: Some dry grass gets trimmed by an author before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha'penny, or halfpenny, is an old British coin worth half a penny, withdrawn in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha'penny was a coin, a 'bit' in the money sense, no longer in circulation.

clue.text: See 1
Highly desirable to get on down etc

parts.note: a plum job is a highly desirable one
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Being on a down-and-out spree sounds highly desirable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like the opposite of up, but it is soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is a bird's feathers, of which down is the soft fluffy layer.

clue.text: Firm runs through claim in court

indicators.note: the runs pass through the claim, sitting inside it

parts.note: to sue is to make a legal claim in court
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A company's litigation runs its course through the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a noun for a business, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure and firm both mean steady and certain, as in a sure footing.

clue.text: Say, gallantry medal mounted in holder by soldiers?

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
the GC is the George Cross, a British medal for gallantry
up means mounted, as on horseback

explanation.surface: A gallantry medal is put up in a display case beside some soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers here are the strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg, a British breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: An eggcup holds a boiled egg, which is set beside toast soldiers for dipping.

clue.text: People long to be muddled; alternative answers accommodate that

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: A and ANS are both abbreviations for answer, so alternative versions give A plus ANS

indicators.note: muddled letters are mixed up into a different order

explanation.surface: People yearn to be confused; offering alternative answers takes care of that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be muddled' gives NGOL, and 'accommodate' houses it in the two answer abbreviations. The surface winks at this puzzle's 1/4, which has two plausible answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Angolans are the citizens of Angola, a nation of people in southern Africa.

clue.text: Book that woman's carrying is in French

indicators.note: in a down clue the woman carrying something holds it on top, so it comes first

parts.note: est is French for is
her means of that woman

explanation.surface: A book that a woman has with her is written in French.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'carrying' puts EST above HER, so it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament, telling of the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: Miss con, starting from the end

indicators.note: reading a word beginning at its last letter means it is turned backwards

parts.note: a con is a convict, and an old lag is a habitual prisoner

explanation.surface: Advice on how to miss out a confidence trick, by starting at the wrong end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a young woman. 'Starting from the end' turns LAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman, as is the title-like noun miss.

clue.text: Sprinter jinks round dog in dangerous races

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round, enclosing, the word for a dog
to jink is to dodge about, so the letters of sprinter swerve into a new order

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A runner dodges around a dog during hazardous running races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jinks' gives RIPRENTS and 'round' wraps it about the dog. 'Races' here means fast-flowing channels of water, not running contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip currents are strong seaward flows; a race is also a swift stretch of current, so these are perilous waters.

clue.text: Town's football team dropping deep, all but one of them amateur

indicators.note: a team dropping something lets it go, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: Chelsea is a London football club
the deep is a poetic name for the sea
a football team has eleven players, and all but one of them is ten
a ham is an amateur, as in a ham radio operator or ham actor

explanation.surface: A town's football team sits deep in defence, and nearly every player is an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping deep' sounds like a tactic but removes SEA from CHELSEA. 'Them' refers back to the team's eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheltenham is a spa town in Gloucestershire, England, famous for its racecourse.

clue.text: A 1A's husband's kid

parts.note: 1A is MARCH, and a March in Little Women is Jo March, so this gives Jo's

explanation.surface: A March woman's husband's child.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo March is the heroine of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women. 'Kid' looks like a noun for a child, but it is the verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh someone is to tease or rib them playfully, just as to kid them is.

clue.text: Might pretentious hosts cut sandwiches and cake at 4pm?

indicators.note: one word hosting another holds it inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: poncy is British slang for affected or pretentious

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: afternoon tea is the British meal of sandwiches and cake taken around four o'clock

explanation.surface: A question about whether snobbish hosts might slice up the sandwiches and cake at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb opening a question but is the noun meaning power. 'Cut' leaves TE, which 'hosts' takes inside; poncy is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Potency is strength or power, a synonym for might as a noun.

clue.text: Couple out of love cheerful after one relatively dark period

indicators.note: cheerful comes after the one
out of here means without, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a couple is two
love is zero in tennis, written O
I is the Roman numeral one
light means cheerful, as in light-hearted

explanation.surface: A couple who have fallen out of love are cheerful again after one dark spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of love' looks like a lapsed romance, but it removes O from TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim time between day and night, darker than day but lighter than full night.

clue.text: Linear C surprisingly needing no decryption

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The ancient script Linear C turns out, astonishingly, to need no code-breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Linear A and Linear B are real Bronze Age scripts (B was famously deciphered); there is no Linear C. The English IN CLEAR also fits the letters, a trap here.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair is a French-derived term for a message sent in plain language rather than in code or cipher.

clue.text: Prank company welcomes 23 1, showing fourfold increase at the end of the month

indicators.note: a host welcomes guests inside, so the rest goes within

indicators.text: showing fourfold increase at the end of the month
indicators.note: the month's last letter, the Roman fifty, is multiplied by four to become two hundred

parts.note: 23 is the answer at 23-down, APRIL
the 1 of the date 1 April, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A company welcomes April Fool's Day, with a fourfold rise at the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: '23 1' is the date April 1. In Roman numerals L is 50 and CC is 200, so 'fourfold increase' swaps one for the other, giving APRICCI; 'welcomes' puts that inside the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a caprice, a whimsical prank or frolic, as well as a lively free-form musical piece.

clue.text: Leaves children behind at home filling baths

indicators.note: the children come behind, placed after the rest
one word filling another sits inside it

parts.note: a spa is a place with medicinal baths
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the children at home while running the baths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about abandoning children, but it is the noun: spinach is eaten as leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy vegetable whose edible part is its leaves.

clue.text: Woody Allen's heart breaks seconds before turning blue

indicators.note: seconds comes first, before the rest
the heart breaks into the rest, splitting it to sit inside
turning a word means reading it backwards

parts.note: navy is a dark blue

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Woody Allen is heartbroken and, within seconds, becomes depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woody' looks like the first name of Woody Allen, but it is the adjective. 'Turning' gives YVAN, and 'breaks' puts L, Allen's middle letter, inside S YVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvan means relating to woods or wooded country, as woody does.

clue.text: Silver darling? Maybe bride expected this to be gold

definitions.meaning: silver darling is a traditional nickname for the ...

definitions.text: Maybe bride expected this to be gold
definitions.meaning: a bride would expect ... to be gold

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into HER RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Herring were called silver darlings by fishermen; a bride's wedding band is her ring.

clue.text: Two classes make up a forme

parts.note: two signals that two words for a class follow; the first is type, a kind or category
the second class is set, a group or school class

explanation.surface: Two school classes combine to form one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forme' is not a misspelt 'form' for a school class: in printing it is the frame of type locked up for a page.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset is to arrange type for printing, which is how a printer's forme is made up.

clue.text: Match up bony bits of 18 Indian meals

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to fit is to match
18 is HERRING, and a fish's fins are bony

explanation.surface: Matching up herring bones from Indian meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is the Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch or snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffins are light meals, especially lunches, in India and Anglo-Indian usage.

clue.text: Temperature rising in sweaty journalist's wool clothing

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising moves a letter higher, to the front of the word

parts.note: wet means damp with sweat
ED is a newspaper editor, so the journalist's is ED'S

explanation.surface: A journalist gets hot and sweaty in woollen clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising in' moves the T of WET to the top, giving TWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeds are clothes made of tweed, a rough woollen cloth.

clue.text: Princess seen on camera clearing lightspeed

indicators.note: clearing something away removes it, so the letter goes

parts.note: Leica is a German camera brand
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A princess caught on film zooming past at the speed of light.
explanation.walkthrough: The lightspeed surface nods to Star Wars, where the Millennium Falcon jumps to lightspeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Leia is the heroine of the Star Wars films, a royal of the planet Alderaan.

clue.text: Spendthrift set get 23 24 with 50% off

indicators.note: to set letters is to place them anew, here in a fresh order

parts.note: 23 is the answer at 23-down, APRIL

indicators.note: half the word is discarded, keeping only its first half

parts.note: 24 is the answer at 24-down, which completes the April Fool

explanation.surface: A wasteful person, determined to fool someone on the first of April, at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With 50% off' keeps FO from FOOL; 'set' shuffles GET, APRIL and FO together.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate is someone who squanders money recklessly, which is exactly what a spendthrift does.

clue.text: Pair tucks into French garlic dessert, a possibility for 1/4

indicators.note: the pair is tucked inside the garlic

parts.note: ail is French for garlic
a fool is a dessert of fruit purée and cream

explanation.surface: A couple tucks into a French garlicky pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the answer 1/4 seemed to promise; 'a possibility' admits it, since 1/4 itself was MARCH PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An April fool is a prank played on 1 April, which is 1/4 in British date order.

clue.text: See 23
Stimulating bar in a pub is where march goes

indicators.note: the bar goes in, placed inside the other letters

parts.note: PH is a map abbreviation for public house
a rod is a bar
in this puzzle MARCH is the answer to 1 Across, abbreviated 1AC, written IAC

explanation.surface: A drink at the pub's bar is where the marching troops head for refreshment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where march goes' is a self-reference: MARCH goes at 1 Across (1AC), with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphrodisiac is a substance that stimulates sexual desire, so it is stimulating in that sense.

clue.text: Clear where to write solutions, except the first

indicators.note: everything except the opening letter is kept, so that letter is removed

parts.note: crossword solutions are written in the grid

explanation.surface: Instructions to wipe the place where answers are written, except for the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an instruction to erase, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of something is to clear it of that thing.

clue.text: Swallow that flies off when gun is fired

definitions.meaning: a gulp or mouthful of drink

definitions.text: that flies off when gun is fired

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' and 'flies' suggest a bird, but neither definition is about birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Slug is both slang for a gulp of drink and an informal term for a bullet.

clue.text: Many 18, maybe the bit of Connery that lives on?

indicators.note: Sean Connery's famous lisping S turns the word as he says it into one with an SH sound

parts.note: the soul is the part of a person said to live on after death

explanation.surface: A wry thought about which part of Sean Connery's legacy will survive him.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is HERRING; herring swim in shoals.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a large group of fish, so many herring may form one.
